notes.summary: Chemistry gives 1–2 questions at NCERT class 8–10 level: atoms and the periodic table, acids, bases and pH, common names and formulas of compounds, alloys, ores and everyday gases.

concepts.title: Atoms and the periodic table
concepts.body:
• Electron discovered by J.J. Thomson; proton (nucleus) by Ernest Rutherford; neutron by James Chadwick.
  • Mendeleev arranged elements by atomic mass; the modern periodic table is based on atomic number (Moseley).
  • Group 1 = alkali metals; Group 17 = halogens; Group 18 = noble (inert) gases.
  • Lightest element: hydrogen. Liquid metal at room temperature: mercury. Liquid non-metal: bromine. Hardest natural substance: diamond (a form of carbon).

concepts.title: Acids, bases and pH
concepts.body:
pH runs from 0 to 14. pH 7 = neutral, below 7 = acidic, above 7 = basic. Human blood is slightly basic (about 7.4).
Natural sourceAcid
VinegarAcetic acid
Lemon, orangeCitric acid

Sour milk, curdLactic acid
TomatoOxalic acid
Ant sting, nettle stingMethanoic (formic) acid
StomachHydrochloric acid

concepts.body:

example.q: Which acid is present in tamarind?

varieties.name: Elements, alloys and ores
varieties.how: Pair alloys with their metals and ores with the metal extracted.

tips: Tamarind → Tartaric; Lemon → Citric; Lactic → milk (lacto = milk).
Plaster of Paris has half a water molecule; gypsum has two.
traps: Brass has zinc, bronze has tin — not the other way round.
Washing soda (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O) and baking soda (NaHCO₃) are often swapped.
The modern periodic table uses atomic number, not atomic mass.

questions.q: The chemical name of common salt is:
questions.solution:
Common salt is sodium chloride, NaCl.
Memory hook: Na + Cl = the salt on your table.

questions.q: The pH of pure water at 25 °C is:
questions.solution:
Pure water is neutral, pH 7. Below 7 is acidic, above 7 is basic.
Memory hook: 7 sits in the middle of 0–14.

questions.q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
questions.solution:
Mercury (Hg) is the only metal liquid at room temperature. Bromine is the liquid non-metal.
Memory hook: Mercury's old name is 'quicksilver' — silver that flows.

questions.q: Which acid is found in an ant sting?
questions.solution:
Ant and nettle stings contain methanoic acid (formic acid). A mild base like baking soda gives relief.
Memory hook: Formica is Latin for ant — formic acid.

Brass = copper + zinc. Bronze = copper + tin. Solder = lead + tin.
Memory hook: Brass taps shine with zinc; the bronze medal is cast with tin.

questions.q: Which compound is known as 'laughing gas'?
questions.solution:
Nitrous oxide (N2O) is laughing gas, used as a mild anaesthetic.
Memory hook: N2O — 'two N's make you grin'.

Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate, CaSO4·½H2O. Heating gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) gives it; adding water sets it back into gypsum.
Memory hook: 'Hemi' = half a water.

Cinnabar (HgS) is the ore of mercury, not copper.
Memory hook: Cinnabar is the bright red ore from which quicksilver (mercury) is roasted out.
